_meta.description: Technology operating temperature ranges from IEA, DOE, and official sources

records.notes: Biogas is primarily an energy carrier; useful heat/output temperature depends on the end-use equipment (boiler, CHP, burner, etc.).
records.official_resource: IEA – Outlook for Biogas and Biomethane

records.source_reference: DOE Biomass-Fired Boilers / IEA Bioenergy for Heat and Power
records.notes: Biomass can be burned in boilers to produce steam for industrial processes. Temperature depends strongly on boiler and steam conditions.
records.official_resource: DOE – Biopower: Energy for Heat and Electricity

records.notes: Range represents established industrial heat-pump and electric-boiler applications; broader electrification technologies can reach higher process temperatures.

records.source_reference: Renewables for Industry / Heat Pump Monitor
records.notes: Large-scale industrial heat pumps are well established up to about 150°C; higher-temperature systems are emerging.

records.source_reference: Task 49 – Solar Heat Integration in Industrial Processes
records.notes: Range combines non-concentrating and concentrating solar process-heat applications; technology suitability depends on collector type and integration.
records.official_resource: IEA SHC – Task 49: Solar Heat Integration in Industrial Processes

records.notes: Industrial thermal storage can use materials such as sand, cement and bricks and can store heat up to about 1,000°C.
These temperatures describe recoverable waste-heat source streams, not necessarily the output temperature after recovery.
records.official_resource: DOE – Waste Heat Recovery Technology Assessment

records.source_reference: IEA Electrification / DOE Process Heating Sourcebook
records.notes: Electricity is an energy carrier rather than one specific heating technology. Depending on the conversion technology, industrial electricity can provide low-temperature heat through heat pumps and very high-temperature heat through resistance, induction, and other electric heating systems.
records.official_resource: IEA – Electrification / DOE – Process Heating Sourcebook
